title: Implement LRU Cache Using Collections
question: You need to implement an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache for a high-traffic web application that stores user session data. The cache should have a maximum capacity of 10,000 entries. When the cache is full and a new entry needs to be added, the least recently accessed entry should be removed. Which collection would you use and why? Discuss the implementation details including thread-safety considerations for concurrent access.
realWorldScenario: Building production-grade caching system with eviction policy

title: Count Unique Words from Large File Using Collections
question: Your application processes log files (10GB+) and needs to count the frequency of unique words. The system has limited memory (4GB heap) and the results need to be sorted by frequency in descending order. Which collection strategy would you use? Discuss memory considerations, time complexity trade-offs, and how you would handle the large file processing without running out of memory.
realWorldScenario: Log analysis and word frequency counting with memory constraints

title: Implement Real-Time Gaming Leaderboard
question: You're building a real-time multiplayer game leaderboard that handles 100,000+ concurrent users. Players' scores update frequently (every few seconds), and you need to display the top 100 players instantly. The leaderboard must handle concurrent score updates from multiple game servers and provide real-time rankings. Which collection structures would you use? Discuss thread-safety, performance optimization, and how you'd handle tie-breaking scenarios.

title: Detect Duplicate Transactions in Payment System
question: Your payment processing system receives millions of transaction requests per day. Due to network issues, the same transaction might be submitted multiple times within a 5-minute window. You need to detect and reject duplicate transactions based on transaction ID, amount, and merchant ID. The duplicate detection should be memory-efficient and fast (sub-millisecond lookup). After 5 minutes, old transactions should be automatically removed to save memory. Which collection approach would you implement?
realWorldScenario: Building idempotent payment processing with automatic cleanup

title: Implement Priority-Based Task Scheduler
question: You're implementing a task scheduler for a distributed job processing system. Tasks arrive with different priority levels (HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW) and execution times. High-priority tasks should execute first, but tasks with the same priority should execute in FIFO order. The system needs to handle task cancellation, rescheduling, and support for delayed task execution. Multiple worker threads will consume tasks concurrently. Which collections would you use for the queue implementation and task tracking?
realWorldScenario: Building production task scheduling system with priorities

title: Build Autocomplete System for Search
question: You're building an autocomplete feature for a search engine with 10 million indexed terms. As the user types, the system should suggest the top 10 most relevant completions in real-time (response time < 50ms). Suggestions should be ranked by popularity (search frequency). The system should support prefix matching and handle typos gracefully. Which collection structures and algorithms would you use? Discuss the data structure choice, search optimization, and how to handle updates to term popularity.

title: Implement Sliding Window Rate Limiter
question: Your API gateway needs a rate limiter that allows maximum 100 requests per user per minute using a sliding window approach. Unlike fixed windows, the sliding window should count requests in any 60-second window, not just calendar minutes. The system handles 50,000 active users concurrently. Old request timestamps should be automatically cleaned up. Which collections would you use to track request timestamps per user? Discuss memory optimization and handling expired entries.
realWorldScenario: Building production API rate limiting with sliding window

title: Handle Out-of-Order Events in Streaming System
question: Your real-time analytics system receives events from distributed IoT devices. Events arrive out of order due to network delays (events can be delayed by up to 30 seconds). Each event has a timestamp. You need to process events in timestamp order and emit aggregated results every 10 seconds. Events arriving more than 30 seconds late should be discarded. Which collection strategy would you use to buffer and reorder events? Discuss how you'd handle watermarking and late event detection.
realWorldScenario: Building event stream processing with ordering guarantees

title: Implement Concurrent Inventory Management System
question: You're building an e-commerce inventory system where products can be added/removed from inventory by multiple warehouse systems concurrently. When a customer places an order, the system must atomically check availability and reserve items across multiple products (cart with 5-10 items). If any item is unavailable, the entire transaction should fail. The system handles 10,000 concurrent orders per minute. Which collection structures and concurrency mechanisms would you use to prevent overselling while maintaining high throughput?
realWorldScenario: Building high-concurrency inventory system preventing overselling

title: Build Distributed Session Management System
question: Your web application runs on 20 server instances behind a load balancer. User sessions need to be accessible from any server instance. Sessions should expire after 30 minutes of inactivity and be completely removed after 2 hours regardless of activity. The system serves 1 million active sessions. You need to implement session storage that handles expiration, supports fast lookups by session ID, and provides a way to list all sessions for a specific user. Which collection approach would you use? Discuss distributed considerations and expiration strategies.
realWorldScenario: Building distributed session management with automatic expiration
